subject: Zero-downtime migration cost pathway and technical handoff
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Timothy Hayes <tim.hayes@novaprod.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novaprod.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Zero-downtime migration cost pathway and technical handoff

Hi Timothy / Elena,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate learning more about NovaProd's inference footprint. As discussed, the core ask from your engineering team is: can we move to Redwood with no user-facing downtime, predictable token economics during the ramp, and an operational rollback if needed?

Attached is a first-pass runbook (migration_runbook.xlsx) that outlines a staged topology: mirrored inference routing, prefix/KV cache warming, gradual traffic shift with canary percentages, and an ops-level escape ladder. We should be explicit about the commercial levers that make this low-risk for you: staged credits during pilot, short-term SLA uplift for the cutover window, and a termination/rollback carveout if latency regressions exceed thresholds.

To move fast, proposed next steps:
- You confirm the 1-week pilot window you mentioned and who owns infra during the pilot.
- We share a line-item credit schedule for the pilot + first month of production.
- If pilot passes, schedule a joint runbook dry-run with engineering and SRE (we can do a 90-minute run).

I’ve looped in Lauren for commercial packaging + Karthik for runtime compatibility numbers.

Attachments: migration_runbook.xlsx (spreadsheet), SLA-diff-summary.pdf

Best,
Mateo
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0124

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novaprod.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Timothy Hayes <tim.hayes@novaprod.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 11:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Zero-downtime migration cost pathway and technical handoff

Hi Mateo — thanks for the runbook. Quick reactions from our side after a 30-min sync with Platform:

- The mirrored routing approach looks sensible. Primary constraints: (1) egress costs during parallel run, (2) KV cache warm time for long-tail prompts, and (3) our internal procurement calendar — we need billing milestones to align with end-of-quarter approvals.
- On credits: we would be comfortable with a pilot credit covering the first 2 weeks of mirrored traffic plus a smaller production-onboarding credit (to offset egress and extra support).

Action items from NovaProd:
- I’ll confirm the exact dates for our pilot window (aiming week of May 11).
- Tim will provide a short list of peak queries (by token distribution) so Karthik can model cost delta.

One ask: can Redwood propose a short fallback SLA for the 48-hour cutover window (we'd like a clear rollback path with defined credit triggers)?

Thanks — Elena
VP Platform Engineering | NovaProd
elena.ruiz@novaprod.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novaprod.com>, Timothy Hayes <tim.hayes@novaprod.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zero-downtime migration cost pathway and technical handoff

Team — summarizing commercial posture so internal stakeholders are aligned:

1) Pilot packaging proposal (commercial):
   - Pilot credit: 100% credit for mirrored traffic up to a $10k cap for 2 weeks.
   - Onboarding credit: $7k applied to first invoice if pilot meets SLA gates.
   - Production pricing: standard per-token rates with a 10% ramp discount for months 1–3 if usage exceeds the forecasted baseline.

2) Cutover SLA / rollback triggers (ops):
   - If end-to-end P90 latency regresses >200ms vs baseline for 2 consecutive hours, NovaProd may request immediate rollback.
   - In that event, Redwood provides pro-rated credits for the impacted window (formula: observed regression * 2x applied to mirrored traffic cost).

Karthik — Tim and Elena will share token distribution; can you model two scenarios (short prompt heavy vs long prompt tail) and include KV cache warm-up time and egress delta? Please keep the output in the same workbook — I put a tab named COMMERCIAL-PLAN in migration_runbook.xlsx.

Elena / Tim — is it OK if we propose the pilot window May 11–24? If that aligns with procurement, we’ll follow up with a formal SOW and a DocuSign link.

-Lauren
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novaprod.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zero-downtime migration cost pathway and technical handoff

Elena / Timothy / team — I ran the two scenarios with NovaProd’s sample token distributions (thanks Tim). Key outputs below and I added the numbers into migration_runbook.xlsx (tab: COST-MODEL).

Summary (30-day view):
- Scenario A (short prompts, median tokens 45): incremental cost during mirrored week (100% mirrored traffic) = $6,200. With the pilot credit cap proposed by Lauren ($10k) this is fully covered.
- Scenario B (long-tail, median tokens 420 with 3% >2k tokens): incremental mirrored cost = $18,900. We recommend a tiered credit: full coverage up to $10k; capped 50% coverage between $10k–$20k to limit Redwood exposure while easing NovaProd egress pain.

Technical notes / migration tactics:
- KV cache warming: expect a warm-up period of 6–10 hours for hot prefixes; long-tail items may not warm and will incur cold-start token cost. We can mitigate by pre-seeding top 5k prefixes (we'll coordinate an export).
- Quantization parity: we verified model parity on our 4-bit q8 path for the primary model; worst-case delta in latency is +35ms, which fits within your stated threshold.
- Fallback path: if the rollback SLA triggers, we can cut traffic back to your incumbent within 30–45 minutes provided the DNS TTLs are 60s or less (we'll validate with your infra team).

Proposed commercial fallback credit formula (example):
- If P90 regression >200ms for 2 continuous hours: credit = mirrored-traffic-cost during regression * 1.5 (applied to next invoice).

Next steps I will take this afternoon:
- Populate COST-MODEL with 3-month projection and the tiered credit math.
- Share a DocuSign-ready SOW draft with the pilot dates May 11–24.
- Coordinate a 90-minute dry-run with NovaProd SRE for the week prior to pilot.

If that all sounds reasonable, suggest a 30-min call Monday to finalize SOW language and procurement milestones.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com | +1 650-555-0189
